description: Fourier analysis of hydrophobic and charge periodicity in the KRT9 rod vs end domains
code:
import requests, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

seq = requests.get("https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P35527.json",timeout=60).json()["sequence"]["value"]
head, rod, tail = seq[:152], seq[152:465], seq[465:]

# Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy
KD = dict(zip("AVLIPFMWGSTCYNQDEKRH",
              [1.8,4.2,3.8,4.5,-1.6,2.8,1.9,-0.9,-0.4,-0.8,-0.7,2.5,-1.3,-3.5,-3.5,-3.5,-3.5,-3.9,-4.5,-3.2]))
CHG = dict(zip("DEKR",[-1,-1,1,1]))

def periodogram(s, mapping, default=0.0, maxper=20):
    x = np.array([mapping.get(c, default) for c in s], float)
    x = x - x.mean()
    n = len(x)
    # power at period p via explicit sinusoid projection (handles non-integer periods)
    periods = np.arange(2.0, maxper, 0.02)
    t = np.arange(n)
    P = []
    for p in periods:
        w = 2*np.pi/p
        c = np.dot(x, np.cos(w*t)); s_ = np.dot(x, np.sin(w*t))
        P.append((c**2+s_**2)/n)
    return periods, np.array(P)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,2, figsize=(13,4.6))

# --- hydrophobic periodicity: expect 3.5 in a 2-stranded coiled coil ---
for name, s, col in [("rod (153-465)", rod, "#b03030"), ("head (1-152)", head, "#777777"), ("tail (466-623)", tail, "#aaaaaa")]:
    p, P = periodogram(s, KD, default=0.0)
    axes[0].plot(p, P/len(s), color=col, lw=1.8 if "rod" in name else 1.0, label=name)
    if "rod" in name:
        pk = p[np.argmax(P[(p>3.0)&(p<4.5)].argmax() + np.where((p>3.0)&(p<4.5))[0][0])]
        print(f"hydrophobic periodicity, rod: peak in 3.0-4.5 window at period = {pk:.3f} residues")
axes[0].axvline(3.5, ls="--", color="k", lw=0.8)
axes[0].text(3.55, axes[0].get_ylim()[1]*0.9, "3.5 (heptad a/d)", fontsize=9)
axes[0].set_xlabel("period (residues)"); axes[0].set_ylabel("normalised power")
axes[0].set_title("Hydrophobic periodicity")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9); axes[0].set_xlim(2,8)

# --- charge periodicity: IF rods show ~9.5 residue acidic/basic periodicity ---
for name, s, col in [("rod (153-465)", rod, "#b03030"), ("head (1-152)", head, "#777777"), ("tail (466-623)", tail, "#aaaaaa")]:
    p, P = periodogram(s, CHG, default=0.0)
    axes[1].plot(p, P/len(s), color=col, lw=1.8 if "rod" in name else 1.0, label=name)
    if "rod" in name:
        m=(p>8.0)&(p<11.5); idx=np.where(m)[0]
        pk=p[idx[np.argmax(P[m])]]
        print(f"charge periodicity, rod: peak in 8.0-11.5 window at period = {pk:.3f} residues")
axes[1].axvline(9.55, ls="--", color="k", lw=0.8)
axes[1].text(9.7, axes[1].get_ylim()[1]*0.9, "9.55 (IF ionic repeat)", fontsize=9)
axes[1].set_xlabel("period (residues)"); axes[1].set_ylabel("normalised power")
axes[1].set_title("Acidic / basic charge periodicity")
axes[1].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9); axes[1].set_xlim(4,16)
plt.suptitle("KRT9 rod carries both coiled-coil signatures; the end domains carry neither", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# Significance of the 3.5 peak: permutation test on the rod
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
p, P = periodogram(rod, KD)
m=(p>3.3)&(p<3.7); obs = P[m].max()
null=[]
arr=list(rod)
for i in range(1000):
    rng.shuffle(arr)
    _, Pn = periodogram("".join(arr), KD)
    null.append(Pn[m].max())
null=np.array(null)
print(f"\nPermutation test (1000 shuffles of rod sequence), power at period 3.3-3.7:")
print(f"  observed = {obs:.1f}; null mean = {null.mean():.1f}, 99.9th pct = {np.percentile(null,99.9):.1f}")
print(f"  empirical p = {(null>=obs).sum()/1000:.4f}  (z = {(obs-null.mean())/null.std():.1f})")
